preconditions.description: The total number of nodes n is between 3 and 200,000 inclusive.
The number of exit-nodes k is between 2 and n-1 inclusive.
Both n and k are integers.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly n lines: one for the distance and n-1 for the edges.
The first line is an integer representing the maximum distance between any two exit-nodes.
Exactly n-1 edges are provided, forming a tree structure.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in edges)
postconditions.description: All edge endpoints are valid node IDs between 1 and n.
The edges form a single connected component (a tree) with n nodes.

postconditions.expression: len([u for u, v in edges if degree(u) == 1]) == k
postconditions.description: Exactly k nodes have degree 1 (exit-nodes), and the remaining n-k nodes have degree at least 2.
The printed distance equals the actual maximum distance between any two exit-nodes in the constructed tree.
The printed distance is the minimum possible maximum distance between any two exit-nodes for the given n and k.
